Financial products (not insurance)

Money Market Funds in Kenya

A money market fund pools investors’ money into short-term, relatively liquid instruments. Funds are issued and managed by licensed fund managers, not by Chestnut. This page is general information to help you understand how these funds work.

Speak to an advisor
This is not insurance. Chestnut does not manufacture, manage or guarantee this product. It is provided by a licensed provider under that provider’s terms, and returns or benefits are not guaranteed. [CONFIRM before launch: Chestnut’s authority and provider arrangements for this product, and add the provider disclosures]

What to know

  • Pooled investment in short-term instruments such as treasury bills and fixed deposits
  • Easy access in many funds, subject to the fund’s terms
  • Returns that vary and are not guaranteed

Who needs it

  • Individuals saving for the short to medium term
  • Businesses managing surplus cash
  • Investors who want liquidity

Common risks

Returns are not guaranteed

Fund yields change with market conditions.

Not an insurance product

Investments are not insurance and carry different risks.

Important considerations and exclusions

  • Always read the fund’s offer documents and fees.
  • Past performance is not a reliable guide to future returns.
  • Investment products are regulated by capital markets and related authorities, not the insurance regulator.

What affects the outcome

  • Fund manager and fees
  • Minimum investment
  • Withdrawal terms
  • Prevailing interest rates

What to prepare

  • Your goals and time horizon
  • Amount and access needs

How Chestnut can help

We can explain the options in plain language and tell you what Chestnut can and cannot assist with.

Frequently asked questions

Does Chestnut manage these funds?

No. Funds are managed by licensed fund managers. Any arrangement through which Chestnut assists with access is to be confirmed and disclosed before launch.
